## Summary of Findings & Implications for the Client

<!-- TODO: Recap the answers to the research questions from the introduction
(demand patterns, hot spots, prediction accuracy, charging policy). -->
<!-- TODO: Translate findings into actionable advice for the fleet operator.
Include a clear recommendation on private vs. public charging infrastructure. -->

Across both reinforcement learning approaches, Tabular Q-Learning proved the more suitable
method for the client's charging problem: it converged reliably across all training runs, 
reduced the average daily charging cost by roughly 22% relative to the naive baseline,
and kept the probability of running out of energy close to that baseline. This directly 
supports the client's goal of operating a dependable ride-hailing service without compromising 
vehicle availability. Deep Q-Network achieved a comparable average cost and failure rate, but 
its substantially higher variability across runs makes it a less predictable basis for a 
service where a single stranded vehicle translates into a missed fare and reputational cost 
for the platform. Based on these results, Tabular Q-Learning is recommended for the initial 
fleet rollout, offering the client a solution that is both cost-effective and lightweight to 
maintain in production. As the client's fleet grows or charging decisions are greatly extended, 
DQN may become more relevant, positioning it as a natural next step for later stages of the 
platform's expansion rather than for the current use case.
